correctness.rationale: The parity axiom gives a row-plus-column binary matrix per pair of distinct occupied classes, with one gauge bit and no cross-pair constraints. Restriction to the actually named base is surjective, block by block, by extending the row and column potentials; the orientation fibre has the difference of the full and base dimensions. Assigning new coordinates to distinguished existing classes or to blocks of an unordered partition into fresh classes gives the displayed binomial/Stirling factors without a factorial loss. Homogeneity and the age property identify labelled extension diagrams with the ordered injective types. For r=2, the cases of zero fresh classes, one fresh class (one or two new coordinates there), and two fresh classes contribute respectively k²2^(2k−2), (2k+1)2^(n+k), and 2^(2n+1). At fixed unary count U and unequal class numbers k>j, equality forces n<m and U/2^(j−1)<2k·2^(k−j). Substituting in the difference of the two binary counts gives a strict negative upper bound, at most −13 for k=2 and −3k²−1 for k≥3 after normalization. Equal class numbers recover n from U. In the family k=2^(g+2)(2^e−1)−1, the change in the power of 2 cancels the change in the class term exactly; feasible bases realize every e≥1. An exact independent integer sweep found 30 equal-unary pairs for n≤255 and all had the proved ordering.
residual_risks: The sharp arity threshold means that the list up through arity one fails and the list up through arity two succeeds, not a claim about the injectivity of any other single statistic. Numerical recovery does not recover the finite diagram or the individual class sizes. The integer sweep is only a finite corroboration.

evidence: Coskey–Ellis Lemma 4.1 gives the two-subset decomposition used for the orientation rank. Jasiński et al. give the age and Fraïssé/Ramsey setting. The EPPA theorem is about extensions of partial automorphisms, not counts of types.
The grid result 801562567ff1 recovers support sizes given base cardinality in a different model with two transverse equivalences.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Structural homogeneity makes diagrams realizable as types, and the parity rank makes orientation counts tractable. Neither supplies an inverse theorem for two numerical counts with unknown base size. EPPA is a different finite-extension property.

value.rationale: The pointwise type spectrum is a natural invariant of a homogeneous structure with named parameters. The nontrivial distinction is exact recovery of both base size and support count without either supplied, with an explicit family showing that unary ambiguity can hide an arbitrarily large difference in base size. This gives a usable sharp numerical reconstruction threshold, beyond recording parity counts already available.
residual_risks: This is a numerical invariant theorem for this limit, not a reconstruction of the named digraph or a claim about other homogeneous structures.
